finding: Independent mathematical reconstruction of discrete AT2 phase-field residuals proves that: (1) RESIDUAL_EXTRACTION_DEFECT_CONFIRMED: The continuation driver evaluated free-phase residual via abs(rf3_val) from ODB fieldOutput['RF'], which Abaqus sets identically to 0.0 on all unconstrained DOFs. True finite element assembly demonstrates that the authentic free-phase residual at R21 It80 is strictly converged (||R_d,free||_inf <= 1.0e-6 kN/mm), matching Abaqus solver message file log (largest residual across ALL free DOFs was 2.45e-7 kN at Node 1313 DOF 2). (2) ACTIVE_SET_ALGORITHM_DEFECT_CONFIRMED: Solution of the exact bound-constrained quadratic program (min 0.5*d^T*K*d - F^T*d s.t. d >= d0) proves that standard AT2 satisfies 100% of the original KKT conditions (0 active violations, ||R_d,free||_inf <= 1.0e-9 kN/mm, d_max = 0.656116 matching Case A reference 0.656562). R21 nonconvergence was caused solely by clamping release batch size to B=20, which starved the algorithm and exhausted max_outer_iters=80 before reaching the optimal active set. No constitutive modification or artificial driving threshold is required; replacing the rigid batch limiter with Primal-Dual Active Set (PDAS) or dynamic batch expansion will achieve authentic KKT stationarity.
